title: Subtraction up to 20
seo_title: Subtraction – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Subtract numbers up to 20 by taking away and counting back; find the difference; use related addition facts. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on subtraction up to 20: taking away with pictures, counting back, missing numbers and number sentences. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Count back on a number line.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Subtracting means taking away. 9 − 4 = 5.
  • Count back on a number line: 12 − 3 → 11, 10, 9.
  • Use addition to help: 6 + 4 = 10, so 10 − 4 = 6.

Examples

Example

15 − 6

Count back 6 from 15

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start numberStart counting back from the next number.
Taking away the bigger numberIn 9 − 4 we take 4 from 9.
Adding instead of taking awayLook at the sign: − means take away.

items.q:
Some apples are crossed out. How many are left?
5 − 2 = ?
items.e: There are 5 apples. 2 are crossed out. Count the units with no X: 3. 5 − 2 = 3.

items.q:
Some balls are crossed out. How many are left?
7 − 3 = ?
items.e: There are 7 balls. 3 are crossed out. Count the units with no X: 4. 7 − 3 = 4.
There are 8 stars. 5 are crossed out. Count the units with no X: 3. 8 − 5 = 3.

items.q:
Some apples are crossed out. How many are left?
9 − 4 = ?
items.e: There are 9 apples. 4 are crossed out. Count the units with no X: 5. 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q:
Some balls are crossed out. How many are left?
6 − 1 = ?
items.e: There are 6 balls. 1 is crossed out. Count the units with no X: 5. 6 − 1 = 5.
There are 10 stars. 3 are crossed out. Count the units with no X: 7. 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q:
Start at 9. Count back 2.
9 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 9. Count back 2: 8, 7. 9 − 2 = 7. Do not count 9 itself.

items.q:
Start at 7. Count back 3.
7 − 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 7. Count back 3: 6, 5, 4. 7 − 3 = 4. Do not count 7 itself.

items.q:
Start at 10. Count back 2.
10 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 10. Count back 2: 9, 8. 10 − 2 = 8. Do not count 10 itself.

items.q:
Start at 6. Count back 3.
6 − 3 = ?
items.e: Start at 6. Count back 3: 5, 4, 3. 6 − 3 = 3. Do not count 6 itself.
Think addition. 4 + 5 = 9, so 9 − 4 = 5.
Think addition. 3 + 5 = 8, so 8 − 3 = 5.
Think addition. 2 + 6 = 8, so 8 − 2 = 6.
Think addition. 3 + 7 = 10, so 10 − 3 = 7.
Count on from 2 to 9: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 7 jumps. 2 + 7 = 9.
Count on from 5 to 7: 6, 7. That is 2 jumps. 5 + 2 = 7.
Think addition: 4 + 6 = 10. So 10 − 4 = 6.
Think addition: 6 + 2 = 8. So 8 − 6 = 2.
Think addition: 5 + 4 = 9. So 9 − 5 = 4.
Taking away 1 gives the number before. Just before 7 is 6. 7 − 1 = 6.
13 − 3 = 10. You must take away 4 in all, and 3 is done. Take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.
15 − 5 = 10. You must take away 7 in all, and 5 is done. Take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
12 − 2 = 10. You must take away 5 in all, and 2 is done. Take away 3 more: 10 − 3 = 7.
14 − 4 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
11 − 1 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.
16 − 6 = 10. Then take away 1 more: 10 − 1 = 9.
Think addition. 8 + 4 = 12, so 12 − 8 = 4.
Think addition. 9 + 6 = 15, so 15 − 9 = 6.
Think addition. 7 + 6 = 13, so 13 − 7 = 6.
Think addition. 5 + 8 = 13, so 13 − 5 = 8.

items.q:
Start at 17. Count back 2.
17 − 2 = ?
items.e: Start at 17. Count back 2: 16, 15. 17 − 2 = 15. Do not count 17 itself.
Think of a double: 8 + 8 = 16. So 16 − 8 = 8.

items.q: Usman has 9 apples. He gets 4 more. How many apples does he have now?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 9 needs 1 to make 10. Take 1 from the 4, and 3 is left. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: There are 12 birds. 5 fly away. How many birds are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Think addition: 5 + 7 = 12. So 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: Fatima has 6 red cars and 6 blue cars. How many cars does she have?
items.e: Put the cars together, so add. 6 + 6 is a double: 12.

items.q: There are 15 biscuits. Chioma eats 2. How many biscuits are left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Start at 15. Count back 2: 14, 13. 15 − 2 = 13.

items.q: A frog jumps 8 times. Then it jumps 7 more times. How many jumps is that in all?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 8 needs 2 to make 10. Take 2 from the 7, and 5 is left. 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Tolu has 11 crayons. She gives 3 to a friend. How many crayons does she have left?
items.e: Some are gone, so subtract. Start at 11. Count back 3: 10, 9, 8. 11 − 3 = 8.

items.q: There are 7 fish in a tank. Dad puts in 5 more. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: Put them together, so add. 7 needs 3 to make 10. Take 3 from the 5, and 2 is left. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: 14 kids play outside. 10 kids go in. How many kids are still outside?
items.e: Some go away, so subtract. 14 is 10 and 4. Take away the 10, and 4 are left. 14 − 10 = 4.
The parts are 6 and 4. The whole is 10. Take away the part 4, and the other part is left: 10 − 4 = 6.
The parts are 7 and 3. The whole is 10. Take away the part 3, and the other part is left: 10 − 3 = 7.
The parts are 2 and 8. The whole is 10. Take away the part 8, and the other part is left: 10 − 8 = 2.
The parts are 13 and 7. The whole is 20. Take away the part 7, and the other part is left: 20 − 7 = 13.
The parts are 15 and 5. The whole is 20. Take away the part 5, and the other part is left: 20 − 5 = 15.
The parts are 11 and 9. The whole is 20. Take away the part 9, and the other part is left: 20 − 9 = 11.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 10. Take away one part, 7. The other part, 3, is left: 10 − 7 = 3. 7 − 3 = 4 uses only the parts.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 10. Take away one part, 2. The other part, 8, is left: 10 − 2 = 8. 8 − 2 = 6 uses only the parts.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 10. Take away one part, 6. The other part, 4, is left: 10 − 6 = 4. 6 − 4 = 2 uses only the parts.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 20. Take away one part, 14. The other part, 6, is left: 20 − 14 = 6. 14 − 6 = 8 uses only the parts.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 20. Take away one part, 9. The other part, 11, is left: 20 − 9 = 11. 11 − 9 = 2 uses only the parts.

items.q: Which subtraction fact does it show?
items.e: Start with the whole, 20. Take away one part, 17. The other part, 3, is left: 20 − 17 = 3. 17 − 3 = 14 uses only the parts.

items.q: 10 − 3 = ?
items.e: The whole is 10. One part is 3. 3 + 7 = 10, so 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: 5 − 4 = ?
items.e: 5 take away 4 leaves 1.

items.q: 14 − 1 = ?
items.e: 14 take away 1 leaves 13.

items.q: 3 − 1 = ?
items.e: 3 take away 1 leaves 2.
9 take away 6 leaves 3.
12 take away 5 leaves 7.

items.q: 13 − 9 = ?
items.e: 13 take away 9 leaves 4.

items.q: 15 − 13 = ?
items.e: 15 take away 13 leaves 2.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 5 apples and 3 apples go together, so add. That makes 8. 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 6 toy cars and 2 toy cars go together, so add. That makes 8. 6 + 2 = 8.
3 stars and 6 stars go together, so add. That makes 9. 3 + 6 = 9.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 8 balloons and 5 balloons go together, so add. That makes 13. 8 + 5 = 13.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 9 balls. 4 are crossed out, so take away. 5 are left. 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 7 fish. 2 are crossed out, so take away. 5 are left. 7 − 2 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 10 apples. 3 are crossed out, so take away. 7 are left. 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the ten frames?
items.e: 10 red counters and 4 green counters. Put them together: 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jump?
items.e: The jump starts at 8. It goes back 3 and lands on 5. 8 − 3 = 5.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jump?
items.e: The jump starts at 6. It goes on 5 and lands on 11. 6 + 5 = 11.
= means is the same as. Both sides have the same value: 4 + 3 = 7 and 7 = 4 + 3.

items.q: Which one says “eleven take away three equals eight”?
items.e: Eleven is 11. Take away is −. Three is 3. Equals is =. Eight is 8. 11 − 3 = 8.

items.q: Which one says “six add seven equals thirteen”?
items.e: Add is +. Equals is =. Thirteen is 13: 1 ten and 3 units. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q: Which one says “twenty is equal to twelve add eight”?
items.e: Write the words in order. Twenty, is equal to, twelve, add, eight: 20 = 12 + 8.
9 + 6: start at 9 and count on 6: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. 9 + 6 = 15 is true.

items.q:
Start on 7. How many jumps to 12?
7 + ? = 12
items.e: Start on 7. Count the jumps to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5 jumps. 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q:
Start on 9. How many jumps to 15?
9 + ? = 15
items.e: Start on 9. Count the jumps to 15: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 6 jumps. 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q:
Start on 6. How many jumps to 13?
6 + ? = 13
items.e: Start on 6. Count the jumps to 13: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 7 jumps. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q:
How many balls are crossed out?
11 − ? = 7
items.e: 4 are crossed out. 11 − 4 = 7. The missing number is 4.
